source_metadata.title: Bleeding and Thrombotic Risk in Low Dose Heparin Infusion as Compared to Standard Dose Heparin Infusion

source_consistency_notes: Table 1 repeats the low-intensity anti-Xa 0.11-0.24 titration row verbatim; it was extracted once rather than duplicated.

The Results narrative on page 7 prints the mortality 95% CI as 9.50-1.80, while Table 5 on page 8 gives 0.50-1.80. The atom uses the Table 5 value because the table is internally coherent with OR 0.95.
Table 2 reports the initial platelet-count unit as g/cm3, which appears internally implausible; no platelet-count quantitative atom was created rather than silently correcting the unit.

The narrative says gastrointestinal bleeding was the most frequent site for both protocols, but Table 4 shows a tie between gastrointestinal and surgical-site bleeding in LI (both 3.2%) and a larger Other category in SI (2.3%) than gastrointestinal bleeding (1.4%). Location atoms preserve Table 4 values without normalizing the narrative claim.
extraction_limitations: This extraction represents assertions directly supported by the article; references were not atomized as primary-study evidence.
The study does not report random allocation; protocol choice was clinician-selected, so comparative outcome atoms should not be interpreted as causal treatment effects.

Not every low-information baseline characteristic in Table 2 was atomized; extraction prioritized study design, protocol mechanics, clinically relevant baseline imbalances, primary/secondary outcomes, bleeding detail, limitations, and disclosures.
No data-availability statement was identified in the article, so no data_availability atom was created.
